# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book explains the method in this repository as the code runs it today (state of 14 November 2026). The method finds subgroups of people (phenotypes) in biomarker data from a complex survey and estimates what share of the population each phenotype makes up, with a confidence interval that respects the survey design.

The earlier version of this book (September 2026) described a pipeline that has since been replaced in several places. The table at the end of this preface lists what changed.

## The method in one page

The data are $n$ sampled people. Person $i$ has a vector of $P$ continuous biomarkers $y_i$, a survey weight $w_i$, a stratum and a primary sampling unit (PSU).

The pipeline has three steps. Each has its own part of the code and its own chapters.

1. **Fit an overfitted Gaussian mixture with a Gibbs sampler** (@sec-formulation, @sec-gibbs). The mixture has more components than needed ($L = 10$ in the simulations, $L = 20$ for NHANES). A sparse prior on the component weights empties the components the data do not need. The survey weights enter as weighted counts and weighted means and covariances.
2. **Merge the components into phenotypes** (@sec-phenotypes). One phenotype can use several Gaussian components, for example when its biomarkers are skewed. FOLD groups the components into phenotypes. Each posterior draw then gives every person a phenotype, and the weighted share of each phenotype in that draw is one draw of its prevalence. The estimate is the average over draws.
3. **Compute design-based standard errors** (@sec-score-hessian, @sec-jackknife). The Gibbs draws do not know about strata and PSUs, so their spread is not a valid standard error. The standard errors come from a Godambe sandwich: the Hessian of the weighted mixture log-likelihood, and the between-PSU variation of the score within strata. Intervals use a $t$ distribution with (PSUs $-$ strata) degrees of freedom.

@sec-simulations reports how well this works in simulation, and @sec-codebook is a map of the code.

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| $i = 1, \dots, n$ | Sampled people. |
| $y_i \in \mathbb{R}^P$ | Biomarker vector of person $i$. |
| $w_i$ | Survey weight of person $i$, the inverse of the probability of being sampled, rescaled (see @sec-weights). |
| $k = 1, \dots, L$ | Mixture components (the Gaussians the sampler fits). |
| $p_k$ | Weight of component $k$; $\sum_k p_k = 1$. |
| $\theta_k = (\mu_k, \Sigma_k)$ | Mean and covariance of component $k$. |
| $z_i \in \{1, \dots, L\}$ | Allocation: the component person $i$ is assigned to in a draw. |
| $\phi(y \mid \theta_k)$ | Gaussian density of component $k$. |
| $g = 1, \dots, \hat K$ | Phenotypes, after merging components. |
| $\pi_g$ | Prevalence of phenotype $g$ in the population. This is the estimand. |
| $K_0$ | True number of phenotypes (known only in simulation). |
| $H$, $M$ | Number of strata and of sampled PSUs. |

The mixture weights $p_k$ and the phenotype prevalences $\pi_g$ are different things: there are $L$ of the first and $\hat K$ of the second. The earlier version of the book wrote both as $\pi$.

## What changed since the September 2026 version

| Topic | September 2026 | Now |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sparse prior | $\alpha_0 = 1$, so $\alpha_0 / L = 0.1$ | $\alpha_0 = 0.001$, so $\alpha_0 / L = 10^{-4}$ |
| Prior strength on the means | $\kappa_0 = 0.01$ | $\kappa_0 = 0.5$ |
| Weights in the sampler | Sum to $n$ | Sum to Kish's effective sample size |
| Label switching | Stephens relabelling | None needed (@sec-phenotypes) |
| Merging | Truth-based merge, or `maxpear` with thresholds | FOLD; the truth-based merge was removed |
| Sandwich | Prevalences only, component densities held fixed | All parameters of a $\hat K$-component mixture (prevalences, means, covariances) |
| Interval | Sandwich plus the Gibbs covariance, then an affine projection of the draws | Estimate $\pm\, t \times$ sandwich SE; no recombination, no projection |
| Simulation designs | One design, 4 PSUs per stratum | Two designs; the second has 2 PSUs per stratum and informative PSU sizes |

The old chapter on total-variance recombination and affine projection was removed because the code no longer does either. It remains in the git history of the `book/` folder.
